key_insight: A lightweight, semi-supervised alignment strategy using Optimal Transport can align frozen unimodal vision and language models with far fewer paired samples than contrastive, fully supervised approaches, by exploiting structure in unlabeled embedding sets.
problem_solved: Reduces the massive paired image–text data requirement for aligning pretrained vision and language models, enabling meaningful cross-modal alignment when only a small labeled set plus large unlabeled pools are available.
method: Freeze pretrained vision and language encoders and add small alignment layers to map embeddings into a shared space.

Use semi-supervised Optimal Transport to compute a soft coupling between image and text embedding clouds: combine a small set of ground-truth pairs as anchors with large unlabeled sets to infer correspondences and drive alignment.
Train alignment layers with the OT coupling as the supervision signal (optionally with entropic regularization and consistency/pseudo-labeling) to stabilize learning from scarce labels.
impact: Makes multimodal alignment practical and data-efficient for practitioners, lowering annotation costs and enabling fast adaptation of large unimodal models to cross-modal tasks such as retrieval and zero-shot transfer.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: frozen vision and language encoders → lightweight alignment layers → shared embedding space

Icon set: low-data/few-shot badge, transport/flow arrows to represent Optimal Transport, and a plug-and-play alignment layer
paper_title: SOTAlign: Semi-Supervised Alignment of Unimodal Vision and Language Models via Optimal Transport
paper_authors: Simon Roschmann, Paul Krzakala, Sonia Mazelet, Quentin Bouniot, Zeynep Akata
